name: cheatah
description: Syntax highlighting, language configuration, IntelliSense, and a file icon theme for the cheatah language (.purr).

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with cheatah
walkthroughs.description: Syntax highlighting, the cheetah file icon, and where to find the docs for the cheatah language (.purr).

steps.title: Turn on the cheetah file icon
steps.description:
Select the bundled file icon theme to see the cheetah on .purr files.

steps.description: See highlighting and bracket matching in action.

steps.title: Read the docs
steps.description: Where the full language documentation lives.

cheatah.root.description: Root of the cheatah runtime/install whose stdlib C++ headers the editor should use for Go to Definition (Ctrl-click). Point this at the cheatah runtime you picked; if unset, the extension uses the open workspace, then the headers bundled with the extension (which the QA gate keeps in sync with the locally-built runtime).

cheatah.purrc.description: Path to the `purrc` compiler used to type-check the open .purr for live error squiggles (a forgotten `let`, an unresolved symbol, a wrong argument count or type). If unset, the extension tries `<cheatah.root>/bin/purrc`, then `purrc` on your PATH.

cheatah.diagnostics.enable.description: Show compiler error/warning squiggles in .purr files by type-checking the live buffer with `purrc --check`. Disable to turn off the language-server-style diagnostics.

cheatah.importRoots.description: Extra directories to resolve YOUR OWN cheatah module headers from for Go to Definition and hover docs (mirrors purrc's --import-root). Point these at the folders that contain your user modules' headers; the extension also searches the open workspace folders and the bundled stdlib headers.

cheatah.trace.resolver.description: Log every module-header resolution attempt (roots tried, hit/miss) to the 'cheatah' Output channel — turn on when hover/Go-to-Definition shows nothing to see why in seconds.
